name: Rhode Island
summary: Statutes: the legislature's per-section HTML (webserver.rilegislature.gov) is constructible straight from the citation and readable by fetch_doc.py, but built URLs are gated for the fetch tool and the site calls itself unofficial/provisional; Justia's 2025 edition is the fetch-tool fallback. Constitution, Public Laws and RICR regulations (rules.sos.ri.gov, constructible part pages, official PDF on S3) are all script-readable. Court rules are long courts.ri.gov PDFs (civil rules 274K chars; fetch tool stops in Rule 26) - corpus candidates. Supreme Court slip opinions are constructible from the docket (Supreme-yy-seq.pdf) only for 2021+ dockets after the 2025 site redesign, with slip pagination; Justia covers 1844-2026. No intermediate appellate court, no public-domain citation, and the docket portal is a JavaScript app that refuses the script.

citation_map.notes: Rhode Island courts cite statutes as 'G.L. 1956 § 9-1-14' (sometimes with '(1997 Reenactment)'); Bluebook 'R.I. Gen. Laws § 9-1-14'. Section numbers are title-chapter-section with optional decimals and letter titles (6A), so the URL needs no alias table. Bare '§ 9-1-14' is shared in shape with Tennessee, Arkansas, Idaho and others: it routes here only with Rhode Island context (context_required). 'P.L. 2019, ch. 82' is RI's session-law form; NJ writes 'P.L.2019, c.82', so the bare P.L. pattern is context_required. A '§§ a to b' range is two sections: take the first. Rules: 'Super. R. Civ. P. 56' (the prose 'Rule N of the Superior Court Rules of Civil/Criminal Procedure' is also D.C.'s title, so without 'Rhode Island' it is context_required), 'Super. R. Crim. P. 32(f)', 'Article I, Rule 12A of the Supreme Court Rules of Appellate Procedure', 'R.I. R. Evid. 803(6)'; Rules of Professional Conduct are Article V of the Supreme Court Rules. Cases: Atlantic Reporter with '(R.I. yyyy)' or '(R.I. Super. Ct. ...)'; Rhode Island Reports (R.I.) ended in 1980 and is the old official reporter; there is no public-domain citation. Supreme Court dockets 'No. 2023-43-C.A.' / '-Appeal' / '-M.P.' carry the docket year (not decision year). Superior civil actions 'PC-2025-03316' (county prefix P/K/N/W + C or M; PB = business calendar) route only with Rhode Island context. Westlaw cites need party-name search (no free WL resolver). CourtListener ids are from memory and unverified. 'Article V, Rule 1.7 of the Rules of Professional Conduct' without 'Rhode Island' is the ABA Model Rules numbering used in every state, so that prose form is context_required. District Court administrative appeals ('6AA-2026-00008', 'A.A. No. 2026 - 48') are context_required. Bluebook page-form Public Laws cites match but have no URL route.

sources.official_status_evidence: rilegislature.gov Disclaimer page (https://rilegislature.gov/Pages/Disclaimer.aspx) and the Statutes.html home: informational service only, 'should not be relied upon as an official record'; 'This information is provisional'; refer to the printed official publication.
sources.coverage: All titles of the General Laws of 1956 as amended, one HTML page per section, with 'History of Section' lines (P.L. citations).

access.pattern_rules: Copy the citation's parts verbatim: title as printed with its letter suffix in upper case (TITLE6A, TITLE9, TITLE42); chapter folder = '{title}-{chapter}' including decimals (9-1, 9-1.1, 22-7.4, 42-35); file = full section number + '.htm' including decimals (28-14-19.1.htm). No zero-padding. Chapter index: /Statutes/TITLE{title}/{title}-{chapter}/INDEX.htm lists every section (not ranges); title index /Statutes/TITLE{title}/INDEX.HTM lists chapters. The section number itself encodes title and chapter, so no index hop is needed. A '§§ a to b' range is two sections: take the first.
access.navigation: Statutes.html -> TITLE{t}/INDEX.HTM (chapters) -> {t}-{c}/INDEX.htm (all sections listed) -> section page.

automation.notes: WebFetch read Statutes.html (search-result URL) but built section and title-index URLs timed out on the permission prompt (PROVENANCE_REQUIRED): use fetch_doc.py. Section pages are small (1.5-11K chars), no truncation. Title index links on Statutes.html are http:// with a doubled slash (//Statutes/...).

sources.title: Justia: Rhode Island General Laws

sources.coverage: Annual editions (2012-2025 seen in search results); current = 2025.

access.pattern_rules: Lower-case title (title-6a); chapter = '{title}-{chapter}' with dots replaced by hyphens (9-1.1 -> chapter-9-1-1); section = full number with dots -> hyphens (28-14-19.1 -> section-28-14-19-1). UCC title 6A has 'part-N' segments (title-6a/chapter-6a-2/part-7/section-6a-2-725/) - take Article/Part from the title page if unsure. ARTICLE LEVEL: chapters divided into articles take an extra lower-case Roman segment, e.g. R.I. Gen. Laws § 21-28-4.01 (Art. IV of ch. 21-28) -> /codes/rhode-island/title-21/chapter-21-28/article-iv/section-21-28-4-01/ (chapter page lists section-21-28-1, article-i, article-ii ...). The un-yeared URL is the current (2025) edition only when the path exists in that edition; a flat URL that skips the article level silently opens the last edition that had that path (2021 for 21-28). Year-specific editions live under /codes/rhode-island/{year}/... (2025 index: https://law.justia.com/codes/rhode-island/2025/). Always check the page's edition label equals the current edition; if not, open the chapter page /codes/rhode-island/title-{t}/chapter-{t}-{c}/ and follow the article link.
